That is, the Brzozowski derivative is a priori not a residual. Rather, it is a special case of the derivative, and under the representability condition the residual and derivative coincide.

This decomposition makes sense in the context of the "amazing right adjoint" to the Brzozowski derivative. The derivative always has a right adjoint, whereas the residual does not. The existence of the amazing right adjoint is not per se a special property of the residual at a representable. Rather, the right adjoint is unsurprising, and the exceptional fact is that the derivative and the residual coincide in this special case.
